A packet addressed to a destination address $200.150.68.118$ arrives at the router. It will be forwarded to the interface with ID ________.
explanation:
To determine which interface the packet is forwarded to, we use the Longest Prefix Matching rule.

Destination IP: $200.150.68.118$

1. Interface 1:
Subnet Mask: $255.255.0.0$ ($/16$)
Bitwise AND: $200.150.68.118 \text{ AND } 255.255.0.0 = 200.150.0.0$
Matches Subnet Number $200.150.0.0$ with prefix length $16$.

2. Interface 2:
Subnet Mask: $255.255.224.0$ ($/19$)
Bitwise AND: $200.150.68.118 \text{ AND } 255.255.224.0 = 200.150.64.0$
Matches Subnet Number $200.150.64.0$ with prefix length $19$.

3. Interface 3:
Subnet Mask: $255.255.255.0$ ($/24$)
Bitwise AND: $200.150.68.118 \text{ AND } 255.255.255.0 = 200.150.68.0$
Matches Subnet Number $200.150.68.0$ with prefix length $24$.

4. Interface 4:
Subnet Mask: $255.255.255.224$ ($/27$)
Bitwise AND: $200.150.68.118 \text{ AND } 255.255.255.224 = 200.150.68.96$
Does NOT match Subnet Number $200.150.68.64$.

Conclusion:
The matching interfaces are Interface 1 ($/16$), Interface 2 ($/19$), and Interface 3 ($/24$). By the longest prefix match rule, the packet will be forwarded to Interface 3, which has the longest matching prefix length ($/24$).
